messages.content: I need to retrieve server responses for certain user queries. Can you send a GET request to 'https://example.com/api/intent' for the following intents: ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye']? Here are the user queries that need to be matched with the intents: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries, such as 'get_balance' and 'transfer_funds'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time in seconds to wait for the server response. The default is 2.5 seconds. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: The user agent string of the software that is initiating the request, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the GET request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to send a GET request to https://example.com/api/intent with intents ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye'] and also provide user queries ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'].

We need to use the get_response function. Provide url, intents, maybe timeout, headers. The function signature: get_response({url: string, intents?: string[], timeout?: number, headers?: {Accept?: string, User-Agent?: string}}). We can pass the intents array. Also we might include the user queries? The function doesn't accept user queries. But the user says "Here are the user queries that need to be matched with the intents". Possibly we just send the intents; the server will match them. So we call get_response with url, intents, maybe timeout. We'll set timeout to default or specify 2.5. We'll use default headers.

Thus we call:

{
  url: "https://example.com/api/intent",
  intents: ["get_balance", "transfer_funds", "hello", "goodbye"],
  timeout: 2.5,
  headers: {
    Accept: "application/json",
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  }
}

But the function signature expects headers as an object with optional Accept and User-Agent. So we can pass those. Or we can omit headers to use defaults. Let's include them explicitly.

We'll produce a function call.
